blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Keyboard trap: Tab cycles inside the open sort menu and Escape does not close it) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap and 2.1.1 Keyboard. A keyboard user opens the menu (focus moves to the first item), then presses Tab to leave: the handler cancels Tab and wraps focus back among the four items; Shift+Tab is cancelled too, and no Escape handler exists, so the only way out is to choose an option, which changes the sort. Remove "Tab" from the handler and close the menu when Tab moves focus out (APG menu button pattern); handle Escape to close the menu and return focus to the button (button.current?.focus()). Alternatively use a native <select> with a <label>, which has none of these problems.
findings.title: Keyboard trap: Tab cycles inside the open sort menu and Escape does not close it

findings.evidence: <button ref={button} type="button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" onClick={() => setOpen(!open)}>
findings.recommendation: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. aria-expanded is hard-coded to "false": when a screen reader user activates the button and the menu opens, the button still reports "collapsed", so its state contradicts what is on screen. Bind it to the state: aria-expanded={open}.
findings.title: The menu button always announces "collapsed"
